- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.2) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior 30d mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 10d high.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is weak or neutral (avg between -0.1 and +0.1) — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with mean reversion bias.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 1st 5 days drop > 2% from peak), reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative sentiment > -0.4), model tends to overreact — apply 1–2% downward bias to forecast.
- When sentiment is positive but price is flat or declining, model often forecasts upward — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overconfidence bias.
